meta.title: Real-Time AI Video: How Live Generation Works
meta.description: Real-time AI video means every frame is generated as you watch — no render queue. How realtime video generation and low-latency streaming actually work.

faqs.q: Is real-time AI video the same as live streaming?
faqs.a: The delivery feels the same, but the source differs. A normal live stream transmits footage a camera already captured. A real-time AI stream has no camera: the model produces each frame as the stream plays.
On live channels, an audience-approved direction becomes visible video within seconds. The H3 Max Director experience streams 24fps video with synced 48kHz stereo — fast enough to steer by chat.

faqs.q: Which models run in real time?
faqs.a: Verified examples from live channels: MiniMax H3 on fal (Infinite Slop, fal.live), Google's Veo (Flow TV), and LTX Video (Infinite TV).
There's a trade-off: realtime channels stream at resolutions like 480p/768p rather than cinematic 4K. The point is responsiveness — video that answers you — not maximum fidelity.
